newsitem.title: INDIA: Kashmir state chief warns against militancy.
newsitem.headline: Kashmir state chief warns against militancy.

text.p: The chief minister of India's restive Jammu and Kashmir state issued a strong warning to separatist militants in the Himalayan region on Tuesday.
"They should remember that those who dug the well for us will themselves fall into it," Farooq Abdullah told a joint session of the state assembly in Jammu, the winter capital of the state.
"The muzzle of the gun could turn towards them also," Abdullah said.

India has repeatedly accused Pakistan of arming and training guerrillas who are waging a seven-year-old separatist revolt in the state. Islamabad denies the charges, saying it provides only moral and diplomatic support to the rebels.
India and Pakistan have fought two wars over the region since the two nations won independence from British rule in 1947.
Earlier on Tuesday, police in Kashmir used tear gas and batons to disperse an angry rally of 25,000 Hindus protesting last week's killing of seven Hindus, officials said.
Nearly 30 people including some policemen were injured during the demonstrations by Pandits, or Hindus, in Jammu city.
The protests followed Friday's killing by unidentified gunmen of seven Kashmiri Pandits near Srinagar, the state's summer capital.
Abdullah denounced Kashmiri Pandits for organising the rally, saying no tears were shed when thousands of Kashmiri Moslems were killed.
"But nobody shed a tear for them," Abdullah said. "Is not their blood as red as that of other people?"
More than 300,000 Hindus fled the Kashmir Valley, the heart of a separatist war in mainly Hindu India's only Moslem-majority province, after a rebellion broke out in 1990.
Some 8,000 Pandit families remain in Kashmir. More than 20,000 people have been killed since 1990 in insurgency-related violence.
